title: Cold spray HEA coating surface microstructural characterization and mechanical testing

preSprayedProperties.Powder_Morphology: globular/irregular, rough surface. Relatively fine A2 and B2 harder particles were whitish and their shape was flaky and elongated due to plastic deformation and fracture during MA. Relatively soft and ductile A1 phase and Cu-rich region particles were coarser and globular in shape. Cu-rich regions appeared as brownish-orange color and the A1 phase appeared as white with black dots due to exposure to heavy plastic deformation during MA. Some separate Cu-rich regions were also observed apart from A1 particles.
preSprayedProperties.Powder_Storage_Condition: kept in plastic sealed containers filled with argon gas

experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: powders with high purity >99.9% were mechanically mixed and processed by mechanical alloying for 5.5h to form the feedstock powder. To assess the coating microstructure, cross-sectional samples were prepared according to standard metallographic procedures utilizing 0.06 mm colloidal silica for the final polishing.

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: All the coatings showed good bonding with their substrates, free of pores and cracks. Mechanical interlocking was also observed along the coating-substrate interface. Moreover, some particles penetrated the substrate and were tightly bound by the material.
